terms.meaning: the dimmed layer behind a popup that blocks clicks on the page

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Overlay, panel styles and close button
sections.what: Creates the dark backdrop, the style set for each edge of the screen, and the close X in the corner.
sections.why: Likely reason: one style table handles all four edges so one component can slide from any side.
sections.watch_out: The left and right sides have a maximum width on larger screens, so wide content may be squeezed.

sections.name: SheetContentProps (part 1)
sections.title: Panel content, header and footer
sections.what: Places the panel content with its close X, plus header and footer areas that stack on phones and sit in a row on wider screens.
sections.why: Likely reason: consistent spacing for dialog-style panels.
sections.watch_out: The header's alignment changes at a set screen width, so changing that width also changes the header look.

sections.name: SheetContentProps (part 2)
sections.title: Title, description and exports
sections.what: Creates the heading and description text for the panel and lists the pieces for other files to import.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard text styles so the heading stands out from the note below it.
sections.watch_out: The title and description are what screen readers announce, so leaving them out makes the panel harder to use.

summary: Provides a panel that slides in from an edge of the screen over a dimmed page, with a close button.
purpose: Lets screens show side drawers such as menus or detail forms.
why: Likely reason: it wraps a dialog library and adds the app's slide animation and a close icon.
how: A dark overlay covers the page behind. The content slides in from a chosen side, right by default, with padding and a border. A close X sits in the top right. Header, footer, title and description parts give the inside a structure.
inputs: The side, the children, and standard props.
outputs: A panel shown over the page.
risks: The close X is always in the top right, so content there can be covered. The title is meant to be provided, but nothing here enforces it.
debug: If the panel does not open, check the open state and the trigger. If the close X is missing, check the content is rendered inside the content part.
